post_text:
I still remember the silence in the room when I decided to step back and let a junior colleague lead the project.

My hands hovered over the keyboard, itching to take over, but I forced myself to sit on them.

For years, I believed that protecting my team meant shielding them from the pressure of making critical decisions.

By doing so, I had accidentally built a bottleneck where every choice had to pass through my own hands.

That afternoon, I watched them struggle through the ambiguity, find their footing, and ultimately deliver a solution that differed from mine but worked beautifully.

True leadership is not about being the smartest person in the room or preventing every possible stumble.

It is about creating a safe space where others can fail safely, learn quickly, and build their own confidence. 🤝

The hardest part of growing as an engineer was learning when to get out of the way.
lesson_extracted: True leadership means stepping back so others can step up.
